Comparing with \(x^2 - 2qxy - y^2 = 0\): \(-2q = \dfrac{2}{p}\), so \(pq + 1 = 0\).

With \(u = 1 + \dfrac{1}{x^2}\) (\(du = -\dfrac{2}{x^3}dx\)) and \(x > 0\), the integrand is \(\dfrac{\sqrt{u}\log u}{x^3}\), so the integral is \(-\dfrac{1}{2}\displaystyle\int\sqrt{u}\log u\,du\).

By parts, \(\displaystyle\int u^{1/2}\log u\,du = \dfrac{2}{3}u^{3/2}\log u - \dfrac{4}{9}u^{3/2}\). So the answer is \(u^{3/2}\left[-\dfrac{1}{3}\log u + \dfrac{2}{9}\right] + c\).
